Sketchbook Archive Looking to move a rare, museum-quality piece of underground illustration history. This is an intact, bound, 111-page original ink sketchbook archive from 2004 (St. Louis era)—and every single page is individually signed and dated by Eugene Rueble! The Work: Packed cover-to-cover with fine-line crosshatching, satirical character grids, wild narrative spreads (like “Mr. Ted's Big Pool Party!”), and raw underground comix energy. Condition: Excellent bound . Every single page is filled, signed, and dated. Why it’s special: A true primary-source document—not torn-out loose pages, but an entire chronological creative portfolio kept intact with verified signatures throughout. author: DAVA Creative Studio
title: Your Photoshop Skills Won't Get You Clients. Your Problem-Solving Skills Will.
content: Your Photoshop Skills Won't Get You Clients. Your Problem-Solving Skills Will. You can know every tool in Photoshop... You can create amazing effects... You can make beautiful flyers... And still struggle to get clients. Why? Because clients aren't buying Photoshop skills. They're buying solutions. A business owner doesn't wake up saying: "I need someone who knows the Pen Tool." They say: "I need a flyer that will make people notice my promotion." That's where you come in. Before designing anything, ask: 1️⃣ What problem am I solving? Is the client trying to promote a product, announce an event, build a brand, or attract customers? 2️⃣ Who is going to see this design? A children's event, luxury fashion brand, restaurant, and corporate company shouldn't all communicate the same way. 3️⃣ What should people notice first? Create a clear visual hierarchy so the most important message gets attention immediately. 4️⃣ What action should the viewer take? Call? Send a message? Visit a location? Buy something? Register? Your design should guide them toward that action. Here's the mindset shift: Don't say: "I'm a graphic designer who makes beautiful designs." Start thinking: "I'm a designer who helps businesses communicate, attract attention, and sell through visual design." That's a much stronger value proposition. Because good design looks nice. But great design has a purpose. #davacreativestudio #fypシ゚ #aigenerated #aiprompts #aiart

author: Wild Edge Arts
title: One last piece of our new identity to share... our Wild Edge Arts brand symbol.
content: One last piece of our new identity to share... our Wild Edge Arts brand symbol. Over the last couple of weeks, we've been looking back through the moodboards, ideas and artwork created by our Creative Volunteers, alongside a final moodboard developed by Jen, who also designed our new typographic identity. As the next stage of the collaboration, all of that imagery was passed over to Aran, our Marketing Support, who also has a background in graphic design. Drawing inspiration from the shapes, textures and ideas we explored throughout the creative sessions, Aran began looking at how these different elements could be brought together into a single graphic symbol for Wild Edge Arts. The final design grew from one of the recurring shapes within the creative work. Aran continued to sketch and develop the idea digitally using Procreate and Adobe Illustrator, keeping its organic feel while introducing an urban twist at its centre, and developing it into the radiating flower you see here. Once the flower had taken shape, the next stage was to experiment with texture and introduce our new brand colours, exploring how the symbol could take on different looks while still retaining its distinctive form. It brings another piece of our new visual identity together, rooted in the ideas and creativity of the people who helped shape it. 💙 And with that, our new Wild Edge Arts identity has taken form. author: The Mechanics
title: 𝗖𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗢 | What We Become While Waiting
content: 𝗖𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗥𝗢 | What We Become While Waiting “𝘼𝙧𝙚 𝙮𝙤𝙪 𝙨𝙩𝙞𝙡𝙡 𝙞𝙣 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙧𝙚𝙨𝙩𝙖𝙪𝙧𝙖𝙣𝙩?” Staring at the people entering the fancy doorway—heels clicking, chatter echoing beneath the bright glow of chandeliers. Suddenly, the cellphone that lit up snapped back the consciousness that had been wandering around the void. One question that starts to linger in mind. A question that mirrors the longing of becoming. Looking up at the dark sky, remembering the unspoken wishes of childhood lying beneath the stars that night. Silently praying for the shooting stars to pass by to fulfill the greatest desire: to grow up fast and be just like them—adorned in bright red lipstick, stilettos clacking on tiled floors, stepping to the freedom that seemed to be waiting all along. While time may feel like it flies for some, the quiet bravery it takes for them to walk toward life’s threshold is immense. A warm ambiance drawing you in, accommodating waiters leaving you in awe, and every savory dish giving you a reason to stay a little bit longer. But for those caught in the agonizing wait—struggling to choose the cheapest item on a menu—every second feels thick, heavy, and frozen in place. And even how many times we want to rush the cooks to serve our plate—life plays you out that waiting is a privilege, and so is the personal growth forged within it. 𝗔𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗳: 𝗪𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗪𝗮𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 After a long queue of reservations, service iced water was handed out. To anyone who found themselves sitting at a table they aren’t sure about, are still torn between the decision of walking away and with the regret still echoing in the margin of their mind; or staying beyond the measure to endure the agonizing uncertainty of the future. But really, who knows what waiting may hold? Is it merely a material success, or is it a deeper, quieter internal transformation? For Reinalyn and Princess, fulfillment doesn’t come from the material things inside their bags—technical pens, high-end laptops, or even T-squares that could bring them a flat 1.00 in their student portal. Instead, it is found between the pauses and unseen moments that will shape them into the person they are, answering the unknowns that could melt the ice that seemed to stop them from moving forward. Waiting, as it turns out, is a process of discovering who we truly are—one that demands something far quieter. 𝗣𝗮𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗖𝗹𝗲𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗲𝗿: 𝗔 𝘀𝗼𝗿𝗯𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝘆𝗼𝘂 𝗻𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝘀𝗸𝗲𝗱 𝗳𝗼𝗿. Choosing carefully what to order in a high-end, fancy restaurant carries the weight of a “once-in-a-lifetime” decision. You may probably have a planned order in mind—but the catch? There’s always an unexpected offer, prompting you to try something new and preparing you for a path you never imagined. In a strange twist of fate of Princess Mina from the Bachelor of Science in Information Technology (BSIT), from slowly weaving the future she once held in, it seems to have slipped away through her tiny hands when the destiny decides that instead of stitching her future she once dreamed of with silky fabrics and sewing machines; computer, monitor, and never-ending coding of her “a day in my life” is her new order. Yet, despite the sorbet she is not familiar with, together with the new experiences with the people she’s sitting with, it helped her taste the future that never crossed her mind. Regardless of her what-ifs and what-could-have-beens, Princess Mina embraced her new path: “I learned how to be independent and rely on the experiences and takeaways I gained along the way.” 𝗔𝗽𝗽𝗲𝘁𝗶𝘇𝗲𝗿: 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗕𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗚𝗿𝗲𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗥𝗲𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 If only the glassware could talk, it would tell you the truth and tales it has witnessed from the very beginning—how others stayed and how some refused to swallow the bitterness of reality. Just like how Princess Mina’s path is redirected, we often feel the urge to try something new, hoping that it is truly the right path for us. But, for Reinalyn Sarmiento, a graduate of Agricultural Science and Technology School (ASTS) now in the Department of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering (DABE), the menu brought her full circle. She may have tested different options, life may make her wait, but she always returned to where it all began—the greens she had always known. While others might spit out the bitter dish, Reinalyn established her foundation on acceptance. She chose to embrace why and how things happen, slowly tasting the bitterness of fate and realizing it takes effort and maturity to appreciate its true richness. 𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝘂𝗿𝘀𝗲: 𝗦𝗹𝗼𝘄-𝗕𝗿𝗮𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗱 𝗦𝘁𝗲𝘄 As the saying goes from What Would Harvey Do, "People who get hit the hardest are the ones who come back the most successful". Success is not determined by how quickly you finish your meal, but by the courage to wait through the brief delays of goodness and redirection of life. Maybe the quick bites rush us to leave early, just to avoid sitting at the table while everyone else walks past with their success. But it takes prolonged heat and quiet time to break down our struggles into tender and nourishing lessons—driving us to feel the quiet idle moments that lead towards a new beginning. It doesn’t destroy us; rather, it catches us when we feel like falling into the void of living out of someone else’s definition of achievement. 𝗗𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗲𝗿𝘁: 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗦𝘄𝗲𝗲𝘁𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗕𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗢𝘂𝘁 After a long season of waiting—a moment that slows down the surrounding noise where the sound of heels clicking and conversations echoing beneath the dazzling chandelier fade into a distant buzz once it reaches our ears—a breath of fresh air for anyone who wishes for silence. The dessert is finally served where you can already taste the sweetness of waiting despite the agony it contains. For the one last time, the phone buzzes in the quiet restaurant, raising the same lingering question: “Are you still in the restaurant?” Only this time, the answer carries the quiet solitude of knowing the peace that lies ahead, rather than despair. A night where silent prayers meet our loudest desires. When luck strikes and a shooting star passes by, may we not wish to rush through the wait, but rather embrace the people we are becoming while waiting for the lives we have always hoped and longed for. After all, how can you ever truly fall behind when the choice of the menu has always been yours? You can’t let someone else decide what you should order, rushing you out towards the fancy doorway of life. You can choose to stay in the quiet stillness, embracing the uncertainty—because the only life that is worth building is the one you choose for yourself. Written by: Jeslycel Manangan Natividad Illustrator: Mizha Ela Kassandra Santos Layout by: James Alfred Papio

author: Martyn Featherstone Mbe
title: Three years ago my wife began talking to a woman in the street walking her dog. They got…
content: Three years ago my wife began talking to a woman in the street walking her dog. They got to meet several times and a story began to unfold about her son, a pupil at Ryehills School who is on the autism spectrum. He only attended school for two hours a day and loved drawing. However, the school could not accommodate allowing him to do art. It looked like a dead end and no future for this young man who wanted to have a future as an illustrator! Then, my wife in her infinite wisdom volunteered me to talk to him about what he could potentially do based on looking and assessing his drawing skills. He had potential and I agreed to tutor him (for free) for once a week for a few hours with a view to making an application to the Northern School of Art. I gave him a sketch book and set a series of small projects with each one building in difficulty to improve his drawing and illustration skills as well as his understanding and annotational evaluation and analysis. At the end, he had a really good sketch book which demonstrated a skill level higher than he would have achieved at school. He applied to study at the college and was a accepted onto the UAL Extended Diploma in Illustration and Animation. He and his mum invited me to his summershow in June and he was excited and anxious to show me his work. I could only give him and his mum positive feedback. He had applied for and was accepted to study on the BA (Hons) Comic and Graphic Novels Degree course at Teesside Uni. Today, he got his results and I am extremely pleased to say he achieved a Distinction. I would also like to thank the course team on that diploma who further enhanced Noah's confidence, drawing and life skills during the two year programme. Autism does not stop young people from achieving their dreams - they just need the right kind of help and level of support to realise their potential. Job satisfaction was watching a student with autism develop from a shy introvert into a confident team leader by the end of two years and having the confidence to move away from home (against Parent wishes in some cases) to study on a degree and then go on to work in the creative industries as Architects, Interior Designers and Product Designers.

author: Art by Lizzie Jayne
title: “The Chief Mouse Catcher”
content: “The Chief Mouse Catcher” The pantry was always full of interesting things to taste and smell—a haven of homegrown delights and baked goods, and often a dumping spot for old pots and pans and bottles that “may come in handy” one day. Peaches loved this corner of the kitchen for it was cool and quiet, except for the odd squeak of a midnight visitor who would sneak through the hole at the back of the cupboard looking for a tasty morsel for her supper. Peaches’ eyes would narrow as she watched a slim tail slip behind the jam pots, but she didn’t chase the mouse off; in fact, she had befriended her and would even leave a piece of cheese on the shelf for Miss Mouse to find. They had an agreement. Peaches would help with a spot of food here and there so Miss Mouse could feed her babies—in return, Miss Mouse would stay away when Cook came foraging for ingredients in the pantry. It worked well, for Peaches was rewarded handsomely for being the best guard cat, and Cook never discovered the creatures’ secret. I suppose you could say Peaches was a good Chief Mouse Catcher, albeit a little unorthodox, but she did the job well, just in a much nicer and kinder way. author: Cameo Anderson - Writer / Illustrator
title: Guys, any recommendations for an electric scooter for running with my huskies?
content: Guys, any recommendations for an electric scooter for running with my huskies? I have a couple of things - I want it to be big wheels (I may not see bumps so better safe than sorry - big wheels are less likely to send me over the handlebars). I want to be be able to let them pull me without using power if they want to sometimes. So I want one that won't be ruined, messed up, or lifespan shortened by running it sometimes on dog power only. I do NOT want a chair. My job is sit-down and I've had it with my butt always being on something. That's why I'm not getting a trike. I would like a basket to carry stuff. Like bottled water and meals for the huskies in case we want to go to a park for the afternoon. I'll figure out myself how to attach the dogs in a way that I like. I really liek the dog powered scooters but he doesn't have electric ones. I feel like I want to have the option to use it without the dogs if they dont' feel like it or it's too hot to run them but I still want to go somewhere. Just looking for thoughts :) We live in town and I want to play with them more. The WolfTrax cart I have is very cool, but way too big to go down public sidewalks with. It's not practical for store runs or just visiting a park. For in town, I'll want the dogs running right next to me instead of out ahead. I love the set up WoofDriver has, but he's often using trikes. And that's awesome cause they have great big baskets, but I'm tired of being so sedentary. I think standing is important for my health. Thanks guys!

author: Just Amber
title: Everyone’s favorite question right now is, “What’s your plan?”. Everyone wants to know wh…
content: Everyone’s favorite question right now is, “What’s your plan?”. Everyone wants to know what’s next for me. What’s in the works? What does the future of Erstwhile look like? So here’s what I have to say. I’m a bit depressed, if I’m being honest. It’s been a little over two weeks since we closed and just over a week since I handed over my keys. There’s no “plan”. There’s no “future of Erstwhile”. At some point I MIGHT sell products online. Or I might not. I MIGHT do some vendor shows, but I probably won’t. I MIGHT decide to take the little bit of money I’ve saved and run away to Alaska (more likely Oregon). The point is that I don’t know. Closing wasn’t a plan it was a circumstance. I spent 6 years pivoting and getting creative. Ersthwile went through so many phases and shifts. So many rebirths and new faces. ERSTWHILE will never be what it was. It’s not a part of my future. It’s a beautiful piece of my past. And I’ll always be grateful for that. But, I’m still here. ME. I’m taking time to heal. I’m taking time to rest. I’m taking time to rewatch every marvel movie in chronological order. I’m taking on SOME carefully selected part time clients, managing their social media presence. I’m avoiding doing work on my house because right now being surrounded by everything Erstwhile was… hurts and I don’t have it in me to do the things I need to do in order to be able to unpack the totes and the boxes. I’m taking my grandma to her PT appointments 1-3 times each week (like I have been for months). I’m doing part time handyman work at my mom and sister’s houses to help them out with their honey do lists and put some extra cash in my pocket. I’m getting ready to help my niece move to college next week. I’m spending a lot of time soaking in the bathtub, because it’s where my brain gets quiet. I’m loving on my pup and trying to find myself again. I’m trying to decide who I want to be in my next chapter and what she does for a living. The point is that I’m human and I don’t know what I’m doing. I’m figuring out who my friends really are. I’m putting up better boundaries. I’m going to therapy weekly again. I’m healing and trying to decide how “out loud” I want to do it. How much do I want to share here? How many people will stick around if I do or if I don’t? I’m just trying to breathe and figure out who the hell I am now that I’m not the lady from Erstwhile. Maybe I’m a writer. Maybe I’m a life coach (probably not). Maybe I’m a graphic designer. Or maybe I’m just some washed up has been business owner who tried and failed to make her dream work. Maybe I’ll wind up working in the service industry because nothing else pans out. Again I just don’t know. I really don’t know anything right now and you know what? That’s okay. It’s okay to not know. It’s okay to be scared. It’s fine to just exist for a bit. What I do know is that one thing has never and will never EVER change. I know that I wouldn’t not be who I am without you all. I know that I love you all very much. I know that YOU are the only reason I’m the person I am today. I became someone my younger self would have felt safe with. I’m deeply flawed but also deeply grateful. So bear with me while I find me again. Thank you in advance. Thank you retroactively. Thank you regardless. 🩵

title: Graphic designers, y’all gotta stop shaming people for using AI graphics.
content: Graphic designers, y’all gotta stop shaming people for using AI graphics. Everybody who uses AI isn’t “cheap” or “broke.” Everybody isn’t trying to replace you. And everybody may not have the budget to hire a designer every single time they need a flyer, post, or graphic. Worry about your work. Serve your clientele. Let the quality of what you do speak for itself. And I’m not just saying this because I use AI graphics. Some of the posts I’ve seen are unnecessarily mean and condescending. title: Hi everyone! I am looking for a new illustrator for the second book in my LGBTQ+ children…
content: Hi everyone! I am looking for a new illustrator for the second book in my LGBTQ+ children’s book series featuring Miss Lexi, a drag queen character based on the one I perform as in real life. I understand that this subject matter may not be the right fit for every illustrator, and that is completely okay. If it is not a good fit for you, please simply scroll past. I am only accepting original, human-created artwork. No AI-generated or AI-assisted illustrations will be considered. To be considered, please comment below with: • A direct link to your online portfolio • Examples of previous children’s books or other completed illustration projects • Links to published work, client credits, or another way for me to verify that the artwork is your original work To help me keep submissions organized and avoid spam, please do not comment only with “DM me” or send an unsolicited private message. That was a central feature of Nazi political strategy: merging the ruling party, the nation, and the state into a single identity. The speech argues that the German people created the state, presenting the regime as the natural expression of the nation's will. In practice, however, the Nazi government rapidly centralized authority, dismantled democratic institutions, outlawed rival parties, and suppressed independent media—concentrating power under one-party rule. From a geopolitical perspective, this illustrates how authoritarian governments seek legitimacy. Rather than relying solely on elections or institutions, they cultivate narratives that portray the leadership as the only authentic representative of the nation. Once that narrative takes hold, dissent is no longer framed as political disagreement but as disloyalty. The massive rallies, synchronized crowds, and carefully choreographed speeches weren't merely propaganda spectacles—they were instruments of political consolidation. Their purpose was to create the perception of unanimous public support and reinforce the idea that the state's authority was inseparable from the people's identity. Understanding power requires looking beyond what leaders say and examining how political narratives are used to legitimize authority, marginalize opposition, and reshape the relationship between citizens and the state.
